description: Comprehensive question bank from FDA_SDA_Computer_Knowledge basic computer terminology notes. Verify before formal examination use.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a computer?

options.A: A device used only for typing documents
options.B: An electronic programmable device that accepts data, processes it according to instructions, stores it and produces information
options.C: A machine that only performs calculations
options.D: A device used only for browsing the internet

questions.explanation: A computer is an electronic programmable device that accepts data, processes it according to instructions, stores it and produces information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is data?

options.A: Processed information with meaning
options.B: Raw facts, figures or symbols that can be processed by a computer
options.C: The final output produced by a computer
options.D: A set of instructions for a computer

questions.explanation: Data consists of raw facts, figures or symbols that can be processed by a computer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is information?

options.A: Raw facts and figures
options.B: Unprocessed symbols
options.C: Data that has been processed or organised to make it meaningful and useful
options.D: A set of instructions

questions.explanation: Information is data that has been processed or organised to make it meaningful and useful.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between data and information?

options.A: Data is processed input; information is raw output
options.B: Data is raw input; information is processed data that has meaning in a particular context
options.C: Data and information are the same thing
options.D: Data is stored; information is never stored

questions.explanation: Data is raw input; information is processed data that has meaning in a particular context.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a computer system?

options.A: Only the hardware of a computer
options.B: Only the software of a computer
options.C: Hardware, software, data and users working together to perform computing tasks
options.D: A single program running on a computer

questions.explanation: A computer system consists of hardware, software, data and users working together to perform computing tasks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is input?

options.A: The result produced after processing
options.B: Data or instructions supplied to a computer for processing
options.C: The retention of data for future use
options.D: A set of instructions that tells a computer how to perform a task

questions.explanation: Input is data or instructions supplied to a computer for processing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is processing?

options.A: The operation performed on input data to produce useful results
options.B: The retention of data for future use
options.C: The information produced by a computer
options.D: A device connected to a computer

questions.explanation: Processing is the operation performed on input data to produce useful results.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is output?

options.A: Raw facts supplied to a computer
options.B: The operation performed on data
options.C: The information or result produced by a computer after processing
options.D: The retention of data for future use

questions.explanation: Output is the information or result produced by a computer after processing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is storage?

options.A: The operation performed on input data
options.B: The retention of data, instructions and information for current or future use
options.C: The information produced by a computer
options.D: A device connected to a computer

questions.explanation: Storage is the retention of data, instructions and information for current or future use.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a program?

options.A: A physical component of a computer
options.B: A set of instructions that tells a computer how to perform a task
options.C: Raw facts and figures
options.D: A device connected to a computer

questions.explanation: A program is a set of instructions that tells a computer how to perform a task.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a user?

options.A: A person or entity that interacts with a computer system or application
options.B: A physical component of a computer
options.C: A set of instructions
options.D: A type of storage device

questions.explanation: A user is a person or entity that interacts with a computer system or application.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a peripheral device?

options.A: The main processor of a computer
options.B: A device connected to a computer to provide input, output, storage or communication functions
options.C: A type of software
options.D: The operating system of a computer

questions.explanation: A peripheral is a device connected to a computer to provide input, output, storage or communication functions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a desktop computer?

options.A: A portable personal computer with an integrated screen
options.B: A high-performance computer for technical tasks
options.C: A personal computer designed for use at a fixed location, usually with separate components
options.D: A computer built into a larger device

questions.explanation: A desktop computer is a personal computer designed for use at a fixed location, usually with separate components such as a monitor, keyboard and system unit.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a laptop?

options.A: A personal computer designed for use at a fixed location
options.B: A portable personal computer with an integrated screen, keyboard, pointing device and rechargeable battery
options.C: A high-performance computer for scientific tasks
options.D: A computer built into a larger device

questions.explanation: A laptop is a portable personal computer with an integrated screen, keyboard, pointing device and rechargeable battery.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a workstation?

options.A: A portable personal computer
options.B: A high-performance computer designed for technical, scientific, engineering or other demanding professional tasks
options.C: A computer built into a larger device
options.D: A computer that provides services to other computers

questions.explanation: A workstation is a high-performance computer designed for technical, scientific, engineering or other demanding professional tasks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a server computer?

options.A: A portable personal computer
options.B: A computer configured to provide services, resources or data to other computers over a network
options.C: A computer built into a larger device
options.D: A high-performance computer for scientific tasks

questions.explanation: A server computer is a computer configured to provide services, resources or data to other computers over a network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an embedded computer?

options.A: A computer built into a larger device to perform dedicated control or monitoring functions
options.B: A portable personal computer
options.C: A computer that provides services over a network
options.D: A high-performance computer for scientific tasks

questions.explanation: An embedded computer is a computer built into a larger device to perform dedicated control or monitoring functions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a supercomputer?

options.A: A portable personal computer
options.B: A computer built into a larger device
options.C: A very powerful computer designed to perform extremely large-scale calculations and complex simulations
options.D: A computer that provides services over a network

questions.explanation: A supercomputer is a very powerful computer designed to perform extremely large-scale calculations and complex simulations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is booting?

options.A: The process of starting a computer and loading the operating system into memory
options.B: The process of shutting down a computer
options.C: The process of installing software
options.D: The process of connecting to the internet

questions.explanation: Booting is the process of starting a computer and loading the operating system into memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is rebooting?

options.A: Starting a computer for the first time
options.B: Restarting a computer by shutting down and starting the system again, or by using a restart command
options.C: Installing a new operating system
options.D: Connecting a computer to a network

questions.explanation: Rebooting is restarting a computer by shutting down and starting the system again, or by using a restart command.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a user interface?

options.A: The physical components of a computer
options.B: The means through which a user interacts with a computer, operating system or application
options.C: A set of instructions for a computer
options.D: A type of storage device

questions.explanation: A user interface is the means through which a user interacts with a computer, operating system or application.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is computer hardware?

options.A: Programs and instructions that operate on a computer
options.B: The physical components of a computer system that can be seen and touched
options.C: Data stored on a computer
options.D: The operating system of a computer

questions.explanation: Hardware refers to the physical components of a computer system that can be seen and touched.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following is an example of computer hardware?

options.A: Operating system
options.B: Word processor
options.C: CPU, motherboard, RAM, monitor, keyboard
options.D: Web browser

questions.explanation: CPU, motherboard, RAM, storage drives, monitor, keyboard, mouse, printer, scanner and network adapter are examples of hardware.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the CPU?

options.A: A storage device
options.B: The Central Processing Unit that executes instructions and performs arithmetic, logical, control and data-processing operations
options.C: An output device
options.D: A type of software

questions.explanation: The Central Processing Unit is the main processor that executes instructions and performs arithmetic, logical, control and data-processing operations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why is the CPU called the brain of the computer?

options.A: Because it stores all data permanently
options.B: Because it executes program instructions and coordinates many of the computer's operations
options.C: Because it displays information on the screen
options.D: Because it connects to the internet

questions.explanation: The CPU is called the brain of the computer because it executes program instructions and coordinates many of the computer's operations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main functional parts of a CPU?

options.A: Monitor, keyboard and mouse
options.B: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), Control Unit (CU) and registers
options.C: RAM, ROM and cache
options.D: Hard disk, SSD and USB drive

questions.explanation: The Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU), Control Unit (CU) and registers are commonly identified as key CPU components.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Arithmetic Logic Unit (ALU)?

options.A: The part of the processor that performs arithmetic operations and logical comparisons
options.B: The part of the processor that directs and coordinates instruction execution
options.C: A small, very fast storage location inside the processor
options.D: The main circuit board of a computer

questions.explanation: The ALU is the part of the processor that performs arithmetic operations and logical comparisons.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Control Unit (CU)?

options.A: The part of the processor that performs arithmetic operations
options.B: A small, very fast storage location inside the processor
options.C: The part of the processor that directs and coordinates instruction execution and the movement of data within the computer
options.D: The main circuit board of a computer

questions.explanation: The Control Unit directs and coordinates instruction execution and the movement of data within the computer.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a register?

options.A: A small, very fast storage location inside the processor used to hold data, instructions or addresses temporarily
options.B: The main circuit board of a computer
options.C: A volatile memory used to hold data currently being used
options.D: A non-volatile memory used to store firmware

questions.explanation: A register is a small, very fast storage location inside the processor used to hold data, instructions or addresses temporarily.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a motherboard?

options.A: A storage device that uses magnetic platters
options.B: The main circuit board that connects the CPU, memory, storage interfaces, expansion components and other hardware
options.C: A volatile memory used to hold data currently being used
options.D: A small, very fast storage location inside the processor

questions.explanation: The motherboard is the main circuit board that connects the CPU, memory, storage interfaces, expansion components and other hardware.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is RAM?

options.A: Non-volatile memory used to store firmware
options.B: Random Access Memory; volatile main memory used to hold data and instructions currently being used by the processor
options.C: Small, high-speed memory located in or near the CPU
options.D: Non-volatile storage used to retain data when power is off

questions.explanation: RAM is Random Access Memory; volatile main memory used to hold data and instructions currently being used by the processor.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Why is RAM called volatile memory?

options.A: Because its contents are normally lost when power is switched off
options.B: Because it stores data permanently
options.C: Because it is located in the CPU
options.D: Because it is slower than secondary storage

questions.explanation: RAM is called volatile memory because its contents are normally lost when power is switched off.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is ROM?

options.A: Volatile main memory used to hold data currently being used
options.B: Small, high-speed memory located in or near the CPU
options.C: Read Only Memory; non-volatile memory used to store firmware or other data that must be retained without power
options.D: Non-volatile storage used to retain data and programs

questions.explanation: ROM is Read Only Memory; non-volatile memory used to store firmware or other data that must be retained without power.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between RAM and ROM?

options.A: RAM is non-volatile; ROM is volatile
options.B: RAM is generally volatile and used for active working data; ROM is non-volatile and commonly stores firmware or fixed instructions
options.C: RAM is slower than ROM
options.D: RAM is read-only; ROM is writable

questions.explanation: RAM is generally volatile and used for active working data; ROM is non-volatile and commonly stores firmware or fixed instructions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is cache memory?

options.A: Non-volatile storage used to retain data when power is off
options.B: Small, high-speed memory located in or near the CPU that stores frequently used data and instructions to reduce access time
options.C: Volatile main memory used to hold data currently being used
options.D: A magnetic storage device that stores data on rotating platters

questions.explanation: Cache memory is small, high-speed memory located in or near the CPU that stores frequently used data and instructions to reduce access time.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is secondary storage?

options.A: Volatile memory used to hold data currently being used
options.B: Non-volatile storage used to retain data and programs even when power is off
options.C: Small, high-speed memory located in or near the CPU
options.D: Non-volatile memory used to store firmware

questions.explanation: Secondary storage is non-volatile storage used to retain data and programs even when power is off.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of secondary storage devices?

options.A: CPU, motherboard, RAM
options.B: Monitor, printer, speakers
options.C: Hard disk drives, solid-state drives, USB flash drives, memory cards, optical discs
options.D: Keyboard, mouse, scanner

questions.explanation: Hard disk drives, solid-state drives, USB flash drives, memory cards, optical discs and external drives are examples of secondary storage devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Hard Disk Drive (HDD)?

options.A: A storage device that uses flash memory and has no moving parts
options.B: A magnetic storage device that stores data on rotating platters
options.C: A storage device that reads or writes data using laser light
options.D: A portable data-storage device that connects through a USB interface

questions.explanation: A Hard Disk Drive is a magnetic storage device that stores data on rotating platters.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Solid-State Drive (SSD)?

options.A: A magnetic storage device that stores data on rotating platters
options.B: A storage device that reads or writes data using laser light
options.C: A storage device that uses flash memory and has no moving mechanical parts for data storage
options.D: A portable data-storage device that connects through a USB interface

questions.explanation: A Solid-State Drive uses flash memory and has no moving mechanical parts for data storage.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the difference between HDD and SSD?

options.A: HDD uses flash memory; SSD stores data magnetically
options.B: HDD stores data magnetically on rotating platters; SSD uses flash memory and generally provides faster access and better resistance to mechanical shock
options.C: HDD is faster than SSD
options.D: SSD has moving parts; HDD has no moving parts

questions.explanation: An HDD stores data magnetically on rotating platters; an SSD uses flash memory and generally provides faster access and better resistance to mechanical shock.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an optical storage device?

options.A: A storage device that stores data on rotating platters
options.B: A storage device that uses flash memory
options.C: A storage device that reads or writes data using laser light, such as a CD, DVD or Blu-ray drive
options.D: A portable data-storage device that connects through a USB interface

questions.explanation: An optical storage device reads or writes data using laser light, such as a CD, DVD or Blu-ray drive.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a USB flash drive?

options.A: A magnetic storage device that stores data on rotating platters
options.B: A storage device that reads or writes data using laser light
options.C: A portable data-storage device that uses flash memory and connects through a USB interface
options.D: A storage device that uses flash memory and has no moving mechanical parts

questions.explanation: A USB flash drive is a portable data-storage device that uses flash memory and connects through a USB interface.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of input devices?

options.A: Monitor, printer, speakers
options.B: Keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone, webcam, barcode reader, joystick, touchscreen
options.C: Hard disk, SSD, USB drive
options.D: CPU, RAM, motherboard

questions.explanation: Keyboard, mouse, scanner, microphone, webcam, barcode reader, joystick and touchscreen are examples of input devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an output device?

options.A: A hardware device used to enter data into a computer
options.B: A hardware device that presents processed information from a computer to the user or another system
options.C: A device that can both send and receive data
options.D: A hardware interface that enables a computer to connect to a network

questions.explanation: An output device is a hardware device that presents processed information from a computer to the user or another system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of output devices?

options.A: Keyboard, mouse, scanner
options.B: Monitor, printer, speakers, headphones, projector
options.C: Hard disk, SSD, USB drive
options.D: CPU, RAM, motherboard

questions.explanation: Monitor, printer, speakers, headphones and projector are examples of output devices.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an input-output device?

options.A: A device that only enters data into a computer
options.B: A device that only presents information to the user
options.C: A device that can both send data to and receive data from a computer, such as a touchscreen or network adapter
options.D: A device used only for storage

questions.explanation: An input-output device can both send data to and receive data from a computer, such as a touchscreen or network adapter.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a monitor?

options.A: An input device used to enter text
options.B: An output device that displays text, images, video and other visual information
options.C: A storage device that uses flash memory
options.D: A device that converts physical documents into digital data

questions.explanation: A monitor is an output device that displays text, images, video and other visual information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a printer?

options.A: An input device that converts documents into digital data
options.B: An output device that produces a physical copy of digital text or images on paper or another medium
options.C: A device that displays visual information
options.D: A storage device that uses laser light

questions.explanation: A printer is an output device that produces a physical copy of digital text or images on paper or another medium.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a scanner?

options.A: An output device that produces physical copies
options.B: An input device that converts physical documents or images into digital data
options.C: A device that displays visual information
options.D: A storage device that uses magnetic platters

questions.explanation: A scanner is an input device that converts physical documents or images into digital data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a keyboard?

options.A: An output device that displays text
options.B: An input device used to enter text, numbers and commands
options.C: A pointing device used to control a pointer
options.D: A device that converts documents into digital data

questions.explanation: A keyboard is an input device used to enter text, numbers and commands.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a mouse?

options.A: An output device that displays text
options.B: A pointing input device used to control a pointer and select or manipulate on-screen objects
options.C: A device that converts physical documents into digital data
options.D: A storage device that uses flash memory

questions.explanation: A mouse is a pointing input device used to control a pointer and select or manipulate on-screen objects.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a network interface card (NIC)?

options.A: A hardware interface that enables a computer or device to connect to a network
options.B: A processor designed to accelerate graphics
options.C: A component that converts electrical power
options.D: A device used to enter data into a computer

questions.explanation: A network interface card is a hardware interface that enables a computer or device to connect to a network.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a graphics processing unit (GPU)?

options.A: A component that converts electrical power
options.B: A processor designed to accelerate graphics and other highly parallel computations
options.C: A hardware interface that enables network connectivity
options.D: A component used to remove heat from the computer

questions.explanation: A GPU is a processor designed to accelerate graphics and other highly parallel computations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a power supply unit (PSU)?

options.A: A processor designed to accelerate graphics
options.B: A component that converts electrical power from an external source into suitable power for computer components
options.C: A device used to remove heat from the computer
options.D: A hardware interface that enables network connectivity

questions.explanation: A power supply unit converts electrical power from an external source into suitable power for computer components.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a cooling system in a computer?

options.A: A component that converts electrical power
options.B: Fans, heat sinks or liquid-cooling components used to remove heat and maintain safe operating temperatures
options.C: A processor designed to accelerate graphics
options.D: A hardware interface that enables network connectivity

questions.explanation: A cooling system consists of fans, heat sinks or liquid-cooling components used to remove heat and maintain safe operating temperatures.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is computer software?

options.A: The physical components of a computer
options.B: A collection of programs, instructions and related data that tells computer hardware what tasks to perform
options.C: Data stored on a storage device
options.D: A device connected to a computer

questions.explanation: Software is a collection of programs, instructions and related data that tells computer hardware what tasks to perform.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Can software be physically touched?

options.A: Yes, software is a physical object
options.B: No, software is intangible, although it is stored on physical media and executed by hardware
options.C: Yes, software is a hardware component
options.D: No, software does not exist at all

questions.explanation: Software is intangible, although it is stored on physical media and executed by hardware.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the two broad categories of software?

options.A: Hardware and firmware
options.B: System software and application software
options.C: Freeware and shareware
options.D: Open-source and proprietary software

questions.explanation: System software and application software are the two broad categories of software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is system software?

options.A: Software designed to help users perform specific tasks
options.B: Software that manages computer hardware and provides a platform or services for application programs
options.C: Software stored in non-volatile memory that provides low-level control
options.D: Software distributed for evaluation or limited use

questions.explanation: System software manages computer hardware and provides a platform or services for application programs.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of system software?

options.A: Word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers
options.B: Operating systems, device drivers, utility programs and language translators
options.C: Media players, presentation software, accounting programs
options.D: Antivirus tools, backup utilities, file-compression tools

questions.explanation: Operating systems, device drivers, utility programs and language translators are examples of system software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is application software?

options.A: Software that manages computer hardware and provides a platform for other software
options.B: Software designed to help users perform specific tasks, such as writing documents, calculating, browsing or editing images
options.C: Software stored in non-volatile memory that provides low-level control
options.D: Software whose source code is made available under a licence

questions.explanation: Application software is designed to help users perform specific tasks, such as writing documents, calculating, browsing or editing images.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of application software?

options.A: Operating systems, device drivers, utility programs
options.B: Word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers, media players, accounting programs and presentation software
options.C: Language translators and firmware
options.D: Antivirus tools and backup utilities

questions.explanation: Word processors, spreadsheets, web browsers, media players, accounting programs and presentation software are examples of application software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is utility software?

options.A: Software that helps users perform specific tasks
options.B: Software designed to maintain, protect, manage or optimise a computer system
options.C: Software stored in non-volatile memory that provides low-level control
options.D: Software whose source code is made available under a licence

questions.explanation: Utility software is designed to maintain, protect, manage or optimise a computer system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of utility software?

options.A: Word processors and spreadsheets
options.B: Antivirus tools, backup utilities, disk-management tools, file-compression tools and system-cleanup utilities
options.C: Operating systems and device drivers
options.D: Web browsers and media players

questions.explanation: Antivirus tools, backup utilities, disk-management tools, file-compression tools and system-cleanup utilities are examples of utility software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is firmware?

options.A: Software designed to help users perform specific tasks
options.B: Software stored in non-volatile memory that provides low-level control of a hardware device
options.C: Software designed to maintain and optimise a computer system
options.D: Software whose source code is made available under a licence

questions.explanation: Firmware is software stored in non-volatile memory that provides low-level control of a hardware device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a device driver?

options.A: Software that enables the operating system to communicate with and control a hardware device
options.B: Software stored in non-volatile memory that provides low-level control
options.C: Software designed to maintain and optimise a computer system
options.D: Software whose source code is made available under a licence

questions.explanation: A device driver is software that enables the operating system to communicate with and control a hardware device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is open-source software?

options.A: Software controlled by an owner under a licence that restricts access to source code
options.B: Software whose source code is made available under a licence that permits specified uses, inspection, modification and redistribution
options.C: Software made available for use without a purchase price
options.D: Software distributed for evaluation or limited use

questions.explanation: Open-source software is software whose source code is made available under a licence that permits specified uses, inspection, modification and redistribution.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is proprietary software?

options.A: Software whose source code is made available under a licence
options.B: Software controlled by an owner under a licence that restricts access to or use, modification or redistribution of its source code
options.C: Software made available for use without a purchase price
options.D: Software distributed for evaluation or limited use

questions.explanation: Proprietary software is software controlled by an owner under a licence that restricts access to or use, modification or redistribution of its source code.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is freeware?

options.A: Software whose source code is made available under a licence
options.B: Software controlled by an owner under a restrictive licence
options.C: Software made available for use without a purchase price, subject to its licence terms
options.D: Software distributed for evaluation or limited use

questions.explanation: Freeware is software made available for use without a purchase price, subject to its licence terms.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is shareware?

options.A: Software whose source code is made available under a licence
options.B: Software made available for use without a purchase price
options.C: Software distributed for evaluation or limited use, with payment commonly required for continued or full use
options.D: Software controlled by an owner under a restrictive licence

questions.explanation: Shareware is software distributed for evaluation or limited use, with payment commonly required for continued or full use.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a software licence?

options.A: A legal agreement that specifies the permitted use, copying, modification or distribution of software
options.B: A type of software that manages hardware
options.C: A program that helps users perform tasks
options.D: A software update that fixes bugs

questions.explanation: A software licence is a legal agreement that specifies the permitted use, copying, modification or distribution of software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an installation?

options.A: The process of placing and configuring software so that it can run on a computer or device
options.B: A change to software that fixes bugs
options.C: A targeted software update to correct a defect
options.D: An error in software that causes incorrect behaviour

questions.explanation: An installation is the process of placing and configuring software so that it can run on a computer or device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an update?

options.A: The process of placing software on a computer
options.B: A change to software that may fix bugs, improve performance, add features or address security weaknesses
options.C: A targeted software update to correct a defect
options.D: An error in software that causes incorrect behaviour

questions.explanation: An update is a change to software that may fix bugs, improve performance, add features or address security weaknesses.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a software patch?

options.A: The process of placing software on a computer
options.B: A change to software that adds features
options.C: A targeted software update, often issued to correct a defect or security vulnerability
options.D: An error in software that causes incorrect behaviour

questions.explanation: A software patch is a targeted software update, often issued to correct a defect or security vulnerability.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a software version?

options.A: The process of placing software on a computer
options.B: A specific release or state of a software product, usually identified by a version number or name
options.C: A targeted software update to correct a defect
options.D: An error in software that causes incorrect behaviour

questions.explanation: A software version is a specific release or state of a software product, usually identified by a version number or name.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a software bug?

options.A: The process of placing software on a computer
options.B: A change to software that adds features
options.C: A targeted software update to correct a defect
options.D: An error or defect in software that causes incorrect, unexpected or unreliable behaviour

questions.explanation: A software bug is an error or defect in software that causes incorrect, unexpected or unreliable behaviour.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a software application or app?

options.A: A program or group of programs designed to perform tasks for users
options.B: Software that manages computer hardware
options.C: Software stored in non-volatile memory
options.D: A legal agreement for software use

questions.explanation: A software application or app is a program or group of programs designed to perform tasks for users.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an operating system (OS)?

options.A: A physical component of a computer
options.B: System software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services for applications
options.C: An application designed to help users perform specific tasks
options.D: Software stored in non-volatile memory

questions.explanation: An operating system is system software that manages computer hardware and software resources and provides common services for applications.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are the main functions of an operating system?

options.A: Only managing files
options.B: Process management, memory management, file management, device management, security, user-interface provision and resource allocation
options.C: Only managing hardware
options.D: Only providing a user interface

questions.explanation: The main functions of an operating system include process management, memory management, file management, device management, security, user-interface provision and resource allocation.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a kernel?

options.A: A user interface for interacting with the operating system
options.B: The central component of an operating system that manages core functions such as processes, memory, devices and system calls
options.C: A text-based interface for entering commands
options.D: A graphical interface using windows and icons

questions.explanation: The kernel is the central component of an operating system that manages core functions such as processes, memory, devices and system calls.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a shell?

options.A: The central component of an operating system
options.B: A user interface or command interpreter through which users interact with operating-system services
options.C: A graphical interface using windows and icons
options.D: A file system structure

questions.explanation: A shell is a user interface or command interpreter through which users interact with operating-system services.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Graphical User Interface (GUI)?

options.A: A text-based interface in which users enter commands
options.B: A user interface that allows interaction through graphical elements such as windows, icons, menus and pointers
options.C: The central component of an operating system
options.D: A user interface or command interpreter

questions.explanation: A GUI is a user interface that allows interaction through graphical elements such as windows, icons, menus and pointers.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Command-Line Interface (CLI)?

options.A: A user interface that allows interaction through windows and icons
options.B: A text-based interface in which users enter commands to interact with a computer system
options.C: The central component of an operating system
options.D: A graphical user interface

questions.explanation: A CLI is a text-based interface in which users enter commands to interact with a computer system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of operating systems?

options.A: Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint
options.B: Microsoft Windows, GNU/Linux distributions, macOS, Android and iOS
options.C: Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge
options.D: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle Database

questions.explanation: Microsoft Windows, GNU/Linux distributions, macOS, Android and iOS are examples of operating systems.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is multitasking in an operating system?

options.A: The ability to support multiple user accounts
options.B: The ability of an operating system to manage multiple tasks so they make progress during overlapping periods
options.C: The ability to connect to a network
options.D: The ability to store files on a disk

questions.explanation: Multitasking is the ability of an operating system to manage multiple tasks so they make progress during overlapping periods.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a device driver in relation to an OS?

options.A: A user interface for interacting with the operating system
options.B: A software component that allows the operating system to communicate with and control a hardware device
options.C: The central component of an operating system
options.D: A file system structure

questions.explanation: A device driver in relation to an OS is a software component that allows the operating system to communicate with and control a hardware device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is booting in an operating system?

options.A: The process of installing an operating system
options.B: The startup process in which firmware initialises hardware and a bootloader helps load the operating system
options.C: The process of shutting down the operating system
options.D: The process of updating the operating system

questions.explanation: Booting in an operating system is the startup process in which firmware initialises hardware and a bootloader helps load the operating system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a file system?

options.A: A user interface for interacting with the operating system
options.B: The method and data structures an operating system uses to organise, name, store and retrieve files on a storage device
options.C: The central component of an operating system
options.D: A software component that allows communication with hardware

questions.explanation: A file system is the method and data structures an operating system uses to organise, name, store and retrieve files on a storage device.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a process?

options.A: A program stored on a disk
options.B: A program in execution, together with its current state and allocated resources
options.C: A unit of execution within a process
options.D: A memory-management technique

questions.explanation: A process is a program in execution, together with its current state and allocated resources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a thread?

options.A: A program in execution with its current state and resources
options.B: A unit of execution within a process; a process may contain one or more threads
options.C: A memory-management technique
options.D: A system identity used to identify a user

questions.explanation: A thread is a unit of execution within a process; a process may contain one or more threads.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is virtual memory?

options.A: A program in execution with its current state
options.B: A memory-management technique that provides processes with virtual address spaces and uses hardware and storage mechanisms to manage memory
options.C: A unit of execution within a process
options.D: A system identity used to identify a user

questions.explanation: Virtual memory is a memory-management technique that provides processes with virtual address spaces and uses hardware and storage mechanisms to manage memory.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a user account?

options.A: A program in execution with its current state
options.B: A system identity used to identify a user and apply permissions and settings
options.C: A memory-management technique
options.D: A unit of execution within a process

questions.explanation: A user account is a system identity used to identify a user and apply permissions and settings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an administrator account?

options.A: An account with limited permissions intended for routine use
options.B: An account with elevated permissions to perform system-wide configuration and management tasks
options.C: A system identity used to identify a user
options.D: A memory-management technique

questions.explanation: An administrator account is an account with elevated permissions to perform system-wide configuration and management tasks.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a standard user account?

options.A: An account with elevated permissions to perform system-wide configuration
options.B: An account with limited permissions intended for routine use without unrestricted system-level changes
options.C: A system identity used to identify a user
options.D: A program in execution

questions.explanation: A standard user account is an account with limited permissions intended for routine use without unrestricted system-level changes.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a file?

options.A: A container used to organise files and other folders
options.B: A named collection of data stored on a storage device or within a file system
options.C: The top-level directory of a file system
options.D: A suffix in a filename that indicates the file type

questions.explanation: A file is a named collection of data stored on a storage device or within a file system.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What can a computer file contain?

options.A: Only text and numbers
options.B: Text, numbers, images, audio, video, program instructions or other digital information
options.C: Only program instructions
options.D: Only images and video

questions.explanation: A computer file can contain text, numbers, images, audio, video, program instructions or other digital information.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a filename?

options.A: The suffix in a filename that indicates the file type
options.B: The name used to identify a file within a directory or file system location
options.C: The address that identifies the location of a file or folder
options.D: The amount of storage space occupied by a file

questions.explanation: A filename is the name used to identify a file within a directory or file system location.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a file extension?

options.A: The name used to identify a file within a directory
options.B: The suffix in a filename, commonly following a dot, that often indicates the file type or associated application
options.C: The address that identifies the location of a file
options.D: The amount of storage space occupied by a file

questions.explanation: A file extension is the suffix in a filename, commonly following a dot, that often indicates the file type or associated application.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of file extensions?

options.A: html, css, js, php
options.B: txt, pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, jpg, png, mp3, mp4 and zip
options.C: exe, msi, deb, rpm
options.D: dat, log, tmp, bak

questions.explanation: txt, pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, jpg, png, mp3, mp4 and zip are examples of file extensions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Does a file extension always guarantee the actual file format?

options.A: Yes, the extension always indicates the exact file format
options.B: No, extensions can be changed or misleading; the file's actual content and format determine what it is
options.C: Yes, but only for text files
options.D: No, extensions are never related to file format

questions.explanation: A file extension does not always guarantee the actual file format; extensions can be changed or misleading, and the file's actual content and format determine what it is.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a folder?

options.A: A named collection of data stored on a storage device
options.B: A container used to organise files and other folders, also called a directory
options.C: The top-level directory of a file system
options.D: A suffix in a filename that indicates the file type

questions.explanation: A folder, also called a directory, is a container used to organise files and other folders.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a directory?

options.A: A named collection of data stored on a storage device
options.B: A file-system structure used to organise and locate files and subdirectories
options.C: The top-level directory of a file system
options.D: The amount of storage space occupied by a file

questions.explanation: A directory is a file-system structure used to organise and locate files and subdirectories.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a subfolder?

options.A: The top-level directory of a file system
options.B: A folder contained inside another folder
options.C: A file marked as read-only
options.D: A link that provides convenient access to another file

questions.explanation: A subfolder is a folder contained inside another folder.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a root directory?

options.A: A folder contained inside another folder
options.B: The top-level directory of a file system or volume
options.C: A path that specifies a location from the current working directory
options.D: A file marked as read-only

questions.explanation: A root directory is the top-level directory of a file system or volume.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a file path?

options.A: The name used to identify a file within a directory
options.B: The address or sequence of directory names that identifies the location of a file or folder
options.C: The amount of storage space occupied by a file
options.D: Information about a file such as its size and type

questions.explanation: A file path is the address or sequence of directory names that identifies the location of a file or folder.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is an absolute path?

options.A: A path that identifies a location in relation to the current working directory
options.B: A path that specifies a file or folder location from the root of the file system or volume
options.C: A path that specifies a location from a defined starting point
options.D: A path that is always relative to the current directory

questions.explanation: An absolute path is a path that specifies a file or folder location from the root of the file system or volume.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a relative path?

options.A: A path that specifies a file or folder location from the root of the file system
options.B: A path that identifies a location in relation to the current working directory or another defined starting point
options.C: A path that always starts from the root directory
options.D: A path that cannot be used in a command line

questions.explanation: A relative path is a path that identifies a location in relation to the current working directory or another defined starting point.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a file size?

options.A: The name used to identify a file
options.B: The amount of storage space occupied by a file, commonly measured in bytes and larger units
options.C: Information about a file such as its type and timestamps
options.D: The address that identifies the location of a file

questions.explanation: File size is the amount of storage space occupied by a file, commonly measured in bytes and larger units.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is file metadata?

options.A: The amount of storage space occupied by a file
options.B: Information about a file, such as its name, size, type, timestamps, owner and permissions
options.C: The address that identifies the location of a file
options.D: The process of reducing the size of data

questions.explanation: File metadata is information about a file, such as its name, size, type, timestamps, owner and permissions.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a hidden file?

options.A: A file that cannot be accessed by any user
options.B: A file configured so that it is not normally displayed in standard file listings or file-manager views
options.C: A file that is marked as read-only
options.D: A file that has been compressed

questions.explanation: A hidden file is a file configured so that it is not normally displayed in standard file listings or file-manager views.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a read-only file?

options.A: A file that is not displayed in standard file listings
options.B: A file marked or permissioned so that ordinary users or applications cannot modify it without changing permissions or using elevated access
options.C: A file that has been compressed to save space
options.D: A file that is stored in the Recycle Bin

questions.explanation: A read-only file is a file marked or permissioned so that ordinary users or applications cannot modify it without changing permissions or using elevated access.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is file compression?

options.A: Creating another copy of a file at a different location
options.B: The process of reducing the size of data by encoding it more efficiently or removing redundancy
options.C: Changing the name of a file
options.D: Removing a file's directory entry

questions.explanation: File compression is the process of reducing the size of data by encoding it more efficiently or removing redundancy.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a compressed archive?

options.A: A separate copy of a file retained so it can be restored
options.B: A container that stores one or more files, often in compressed form, such as ZIP or 7z
options.C: A link that provides convenient access to another file
options.D: A file marked as read-only

questions.explanation: A compressed archive is a container that stores one or more files, often in compressed form, such as ZIP or 7z.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a backup file?

options.A: A file that is not displayed in standard file listings
options.B: A separate copy of a file or data set retained so it can be restored if the original is lost or damaged
options.C: A file marked as read-only
options.D: A container that stores files in compressed form

questions.explanation: A backup file is a separate copy of a file or data set retained so it can be restored if the original is lost or damaged.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is file copying?

options.A: Changing a file's location
options.B: Creating another copy of a file at a different or the same storage location
options.C: Changing the name of a file without changing its contents
options.D: Removing a file's directory entry

questions.explanation: File copying is creating another copy of a file at a different or the same storage location.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is file moving?

options.A: Creating another copy of a file at a different location
options.B: Changing a file's location; depending on the file system and operation, this may involve updating directory information or copying and deleting data
options.C: Changing the name of a file without changing its contents
options.D: Removing a file's directory entry

questions.explanation: File moving is changing a file's location; depending on the file system and operation, this may involve updating directory information or copying and deleting data.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is file renaming?

options.A: Changing a file's location
options.B: Changing the name of a file without necessarily changing its contents
options.C: Creating another copy of a file
options.D: Removing a file's directory entry

questions.explanation: File renaming is changing the name of a file without necessarily changing its contents.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is file deletion?

options.A: Creating another copy of a file at a different location
options.B: Removing a file's directory entry or marking its storage space as reusable; secure erasure requires additional measures
options.C: Changing the name of a file
options.D: Reducing the size of data by encoding it more efficiently

questions.explanation: File deletion is removing a file's directory entry or marking its storage space as reusable; secure erasure requires additional measures.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is the Recycle Bin in Windows?

options.A: A folder that stores all files permanently
options.B: A temporary location that commonly holds deleted local files so they can be restored or permanently removed, subject to deletion method and settings
options.C: A tool for compressing files
options.D: A link that provides access to another file

questions.explanation: The Recycle Bin in Windows is a temporary location that commonly holds deleted local files so they can be restored or permanently removed, subject to deletion method and settings.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a file permission?

options.A: A rule that determines which users or groups can read, write, execute or otherwise access a file
options.B: A link that provides convenient access to another file
options.C: A separate copy of a file retained for restoration
options.D: A container that stores files in compressed form

questions.explanation: A file permission is a rule that determines which users or groups can read, write, execute or otherwise access a file.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a file shortcut?

options.A: A separate copy of a file retained for restoration
options.B: A link or reference that provides convenient access to another file, folder or program without being the original item
options.C: A rule that determines who can access a file
options.D: A container that stores files in compressed form

questions.explanation: A file shortcut is a link or reference that provides convenient access to another file, folder or program without being the original item.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a database?

options.A: A file stored on a storage device
options.B: An organised collection of data stored and managed so that it can be accessed, updated and retrieved efficiently
options.C: Software used to create documents
options.D: A network of computers

questions.explanation: A database is an organised collection of data stored and managed so that it can be accessed, updated and retrieved efficiently.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Database Management System (DBMS)?

options.A: An organised collection of data
options.B: Software used to define, create, store, retrieve, update and administer databases
options.C: A file system structure
options.D: A type of network protocol

questions.explanation: A Database Management System is software used to define, create, store, retrieve, update and administer databases.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: Which of the following are examples of DBMS software?

options.A: Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint
options.B: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle Database, Microsoft SQL Server, SQLite and MariaDB
options.C: Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox, Microsoft Edge
options.D: Windows, Linux, macOS

questions.explanation: MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle Database, Microsoft SQL Server, SQLite and MariaDB are examples of DBMS software.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a Relational Database Management System (RDBMS)?

options.A: A DBMS that organises data primarily into related tables made up of rows and columns
options.B: A DBMS that uses document, key-value or graph models
options.C: Software used to create spreadsheets
options.D: A type of network protocol

questions.explanation: A Relational Database Management System is a DBMS that organises data primarily into related tables made up of rows and columns.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a table in a relational database?

options.A: A single data element or attribute
options.B: A structured collection of related records organised into rows and columns
options.C: A request to retrieve data
options.D: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval

questions.explanation: A table in a relational database is a structured collection of related records organised into rows and columns.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a column in a database table?

options.A: A record containing values for one item
options.B: A field that stores a particular attribute for records in the table
options.C: A request to retrieve data
options.D: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval

questions.explanation: A column in a database table is a field that stores a particular attribute for records in the table.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a record?

options.A: A single data element or attribute
options.B: A collection of related field values describing one entity or instance in a database
options.C: A request to retrieve data
options.D: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval

questions.explanation: A record is a collection of related field values describing one entity or instance in a database.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a field?

options.A: A single data element or attribute in a record or table column
options.B: A collection of related records
options.C: A request to retrieve data
options.D: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval

questions.explanation: A field is a single data element or attribute in a record or table column.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a primary key?

options.A: A column or set of columns that refers to a key in another table
options.B: A column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a table and cannot contain duplicate key values
options.C: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval
options.D: A logical unit of database work

questions.explanation: A primary key is a column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a table and cannot contain duplicate key values.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a foreign key?

options.A: A column or set of columns that uniquely identifies each row in a table
options.B: A column or set of columns that refers to a candidate or primary key in another or the same table to establish a relationship
options.C: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval
options.D: A logical unit of database work

questions.explanation: A foreign key is a column or set of columns that refers to a candidate or primary key in another or the same table to establish a relationship.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a database query?

options.A: A formatted presentation of selected database information
options.B: A request to retrieve, insert, update, delete or otherwise manipulate data in a database
options.C: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval
options.D: A logical unit of database work

questions.explanation: A database query is a request to retrieve, insert, update, delete or otherwise manipulate data in a database.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is SQL?

options.A: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval
options.B: Structured Query Language, a language commonly used to define, query and manipulate relational databases
options.C: A logical unit of database work
options.D: A user interface used to enter database records

questions.explanation: SQL stands for Structured Query Language, a language commonly used to define, query and manipulate relational databases.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does SELECT do in SQL?

options.A: Adds new rows to a database table
options.B: Retrieves data from one or more database tables or other query sources
options.C: Modifies existing rows in a database table
options.D: Removes selected rows from a database table

questions.explanation: SELECT retrieves data from one or more database tables or other query sources.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does INSERT do in SQL?

options.A: Retrieves data from a table
options.B: Adds new rows to a database table
options.C: Modifies existing rows in a database table
options.D: Removes selected rows from a database table

questions.explanation: INSERT adds new rows to a database table.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does UPDATE do in SQL?

options.A: Retrieves data from a table
options.B: Adds new rows to a database table
options.C: Modifies existing rows in a database table
options.D: Removes selected rows from a database table

questions.explanation: UPDATE modifies existing rows in a database table.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What does DELETE do in SQL?

options.A: Retrieves data from a table
options.B: Adds new rows to a database table
options.C: Modifies existing rows in a database table
options.D: Removes selected rows from a database table

questions.explanation: DELETE removes selected rows from a database table.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a database form?

options.A: A formatted presentation of selected database information
options.B: A user interface used to enter, view or edit database records
options.C: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval
options.D: A logical unit of database work

questions.explanation: A database form is a user interface used to enter, view or edit database records.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a database report?

options.A: A user interface used to enter database records
options.B: A formatted presentation of selected database information, often designed for viewing or printing
options.C: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval
options.D: A logical unit of database work

questions.explanation: A database report is a formatted presentation of selected database information, often designed for viewing or printing.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a database index?

options.A: A user interface used to enter database records
options.B: A data structure that can speed up data retrieval from a table, usually at the cost of additional storage and maintenance
options.C: A formatted presentation of selected database information
options.D: A logical unit of database work

questions.explanation: A database index is a data structure that can speed up data retrieval from a table, usually at the cost of additional storage and maintenance.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is database normalisation?

options.A: The process of structuring relational tables to reduce unnecessary duplication and improve data integrity
options.B: The process of creating a backup copy of the database
options.C: The process of indexing data for faster retrieval
options.D: The process of encrypting database records

questions.explanation: Database normalisation is the process of structuring relational tables to reduce unnecessary duplication and improve data integrity.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is data redundancy?

options.A: The accuracy and consistency of stored data
options.B: Unnecessary duplication of the same data in multiple places
options.C: A logical unit of database work
options.D: A data structure that speeds up retrieval

questions.explanation: Data redundancy is unnecessary duplication of the same data in multiple places.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is data integrity in a database?

options.A: Unnecessary duplication of the same data
options.B: The accuracy, consistency and reliability of stored data, supported by constraints and validation rules
options.C: A logical unit of database work
options.D: A data structure that speeds up retrieval

questions.explanation: Data integrity in a database is the accuracy, consistency and reliability of stored data, supported by constraints and validation rules.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a database transaction?

options.A: A copy of database data used to restore the database
options.B: A logical unit of database work that is treated as a single operation or set of operations
options.C: A data structure that speeds up data retrieval
options.D: A user interface used to enter database records

questions.explanation: A database transaction is a logical unit of database work that is treated as a single operation or set of operations.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What are ACID properties in database transactions?

options.A: Access, Consistency, Integrity, Durability
options.B: Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and Durability
options.C: Accuracy, Consistency, Isolation, Dependency
options.D: Atomicity, Control, Integrity, Data

questions.explanation: ACID properties in database transactions are Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation and Durability.

questions.subject: Computer Knowledge
questions.question: What is a database backup?

options.A: A logical unit of database work
